explain.say: Imagine your friend Ravi in Mumbai says his school bag hurts his shoulders. You could guess a fix, but great designers start somewhere surprising: with the person. Look at the circle on the board. Step one is empathise, which means trying to feel what someone else feels.

explain.say: So you watch Ravi walk to school and ask questions. You learn the bag is heavy on one side. Now look at define: write the real problem in one sentence. Ravi needs a bag that spreads the weight evenly. Why is one clear sentence so useful?

explain.say: Look at ideate, which means coming up with ideas. Sketch lots of them, even silly ones: wheels, two straps, a belly strap, pockets for heavy books close to the back. More ideas means more chances for a great one. How many ideas could you sketch in five minutes?

faq.q: What does empathise mean in design?
faq.a: Empathise means understanding the people you are designing for by watching, listening and asking questions, so you know their real needs and feelings.
Ideate means coming up with lots of ideas, without judging them at first. Wild ideas are welcome, because they can lead to clever solutions.
A prototype is a quick, simple model of an idea, made to test it. It can be made of card, clay, tape or even drawn on paper for an app.
Testing always shows something to improve, so designers go back, change the design and test again. Repeating like this is called iteration.
Design thinking is a way of solving problems that starts with people's needs and goes through five stages: empathise, define, ideate, prototype and test, often looping round.
asks: What are the five stages of design thinking?

facts: The five-stage design thinking model, empathise, define, ideate, prototype and test, was popularised by the Hasso Plattner Institute of Design at Stanford (the d.school).
James Dyson says he made 5,127 prototypes before creating his first working bagless vacuum cleaner.

quiz.say: Which stage of design thinking comes first?
quiz.why: You first understand the people you are designing for.

wrong.1: You prototype after you have defined the problem and had ideas.
wrong.2: Testing comes once you have something to try.

quiz.say: Your prototype bag fails its test. What should a designer do?

options.show: Learn from it and improve the design
options.say: Learn from it and improve the design

quiz.why: Design is a loop: each test teaches you how to make it better.

wrong.1: Failed tests are normal and useful.
wrong.2: Selling a design that does not work would let people down.
